page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7571 processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 96 virtual CPUs and 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 3600 GB of bundled NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance tradeoffs for this hardware configuration. Single-core processing capabilities are limited, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded compression tests consistently ranking in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core performance is more robust, achieving average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory performance is a notable strength, with small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth placing in the top 25%, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths remain average. Additionally, the processor demonstrates strong capabilities in cryptographic operations and ray tracing benchmarks, though large-scale LLM inference tasks show weaker performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m5ad.24xlarge delivers a high density of physical cores and memory alongside integrated local NVMe storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput tasks. This resource profile is well-suited for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage the high core count and local SSD storage. Appropriate applications include relational databases, distributed data stores, static web serving, and multi-threaded batch processing, whereas single-threaded applications or heavy LLM inference tasks may not utilize the hardware efficiently.
